question.problem: Find all the real solutions to the equation $5{b}^{3}+12{b}^{2}+20b+48=0.$
question.worked_solution:
We proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{b}^{3}+12{b}^{2}+20b+48 & = \\ (5{b}^{3}+12{b}^{2})+(20b+48) & = \\ {b}^{2}(5b+12)+4(5b+12) & = \\ (5b+12)\cdot {b}^{2}+(5b+12)\cdot 4 & = \\ (5b+12)({b}^{2}+4) & .\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve $(5b+12)({b}^{2}+4)=0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

- Setting the factor $(5b+12)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5b+12 & =0 \\ 5b & =-12 \\ b & =-\frac{12}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $({b}^{2}+4)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}^{2}+4 & =0 \\ {b}^{2} & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since a squared real number cannot be negative, the equation ${b}^{2}+4=0$ has no real solutions.

Therefore,  $b=-\frac{12}{5}$ is the only real solution.
